speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Prime Minister (a) whether the Government plans to include climate risk, particularly climate change-related risk, in the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS’) annual Industry-Wide Stress Test (IWST), in line with what the Bank of England is doing and what the International Monetary Fund (IMF) recommends for central banks; and (b) if not, why the Government is choosing not to do so.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Financial institutions are potentially exposed to such risks because they provide financing and insurance services to businesses that can be impacted by a wide range of climate change-related events, including natural catastrophes.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: There are also risks arising from changes to public policies, technologies or consumer preferences that can impact businesses significantly.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: Climate change is, therefore, increasingly relevant to financial institutions, both because the risks will be on their balance sheets and because they will play a role in enabling their customers and the economy at large to make a transition here in Singapore as well as abroad.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: MAS is, in fact, a founding member of the global Network for Greening the Financial System, which develops best practices for a more sustainable financial industry.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: But the methodologies for stress testing climate change-related risk are still at a nascent stage, as international regulators all recognise.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: The Bank of England, as mentioned by Mr Louis Ng, has acknowledged that central banks and the financial sector are still building capacity to model financial risks arising from climate change.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung) (for the Prime Minister)
text: IMF, too, is working to improve its climate change-related stress scenarios.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Just one follow-up question, I am just wondering whether we can also get our financial institutions to report on the amount of emissions they are financing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That way, we can also see just how at-risk they are.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I think many of our financial institutions see it as in their own interest to report it because shareholders and stakeholders are all watching the data.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the end, this will succeed when we can converge commercial interest with social good and environmental good.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What is very positive and optimistic is that such a convergence is happening.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When it is all worked out, I am sure then there will be more conversations, including with civil society.
